beefs.title: Multiplication
beefs.about: Added the correct statement that the commutative property does not hold when we multiply a natural number n greater than or equal to 1 by 0. This follows directly from the fact that if we physically hold some object and we want to multiply it by 0, the object will not disappear; therefore, 0*n is undefined. Whereas, if we do not have any object and we want to multiply it by n, the result will always be 0. In other words, n*0 != 0*n.
